title: They Abandoned a Ship That Couldn't Sink — 25 People Vanished Without a Trace
description:
On October 3rd, 1955, the MV Joyita left Apia, Samoa with 25 people aboard — crew, a government official, a doctor, and two children — bound for the Tokelau Islands. The 270-mile trip should have taken 41 hours. She never arrived.

Thirty-seven days later, a merchant ship found her drifting 600 miles off course, half-flooded and listing hard — but completely empty. Blood-soaked bandages, a torn medical bag, and a stopped clock at 10:25 were the only clues left behind. Every lifeboat and life raft was gone. So were 22 of the 25 life jackets.

Here's what makes it truly bizarre: the Joyita couldn't sink. Her hull was packed with cork insulation, keeping her afloat even half-flooded. So why would 25 people abandon a ship that never actually went under? No bodies were ever found. No wreckage. No survivors. Just an unsolved mystery the Pacific has never given back.
